## Introducing the InnovateUS Spring 2026 Workshop Season
 
 *Date: 2025-12-15 10:00:00*
 
 *Tags: ["AI for Governance","Governing AI","AI and Service Delivery","AI Tools","AI and Problem Solving","AI and Public Engagement","AI Infrastructure","AI and Law","AI and Labor","AI and Education","AI and Public Safety","AI and Lawmaking"]*
 
 ### Excerpt
 
 InnovateUS has become a backbone of AI capacity-building in government, helping public servants move past hype toward practical, responsible use. This spring, InnovateUS launches its largest workshop season yet, convening leading voices in public-sector AI to tackle the real decisions agencies face: procurement, governance, communication, service delivery, and workforce impact. From predictive systems to public AI infrastructure, the Spring 2026 series is designed to strengthen human judgment, public trust, and democratic capacity in an AI-driven era.
 
 ### Content
 
 Every day, public servants across the country are asked to navigate a rapidly changing AI landscape while keeping government services running seamlessly. InnovateUS exists to make that work easier. The mission is to provide public-sector professionals with practical, usable, human-centered tools to understand AI, govern it responsibly, and apply it to real public challenges. Over the past year, InnovateUS has become a backbone of AI capacity-building in government, helping agencies build the skills and judgment needed to adopt emerging technologies responsibly. This spring's lineup brings together some of the most respected voices in public-sector AI and innovation—including Beth Simone Noveck, Arvind Narayanan, Christian Bason, Deborah Stine, and more—to help public servants across the country chart the path forward. Whether you're a state chief information officer, a benefits caseworker, an agency communicator, or a city innovation lead, there's a place for you to engage, learn, and grow. Read more to learn how InnovateUS designed the workshop series. What InnovateUS Workshops Offer InnovateUS workshops are designed for real work in real government settings. Sessions are: Free and open to any public servant Taught by national experts and leading practitioners Hands-on, plain-language, and grounded in real case studies Focused on skills, not hype Participants gain frameworks, prompts, examples, templates, and tested practices they can bring back to their teams the same day; workshops run live on Zoom, with recordings available. The Spring 2026 season features weekly sessions from January through June, including our signature Prompting Lab, returning favorites such as Amplify, and several new series on AI governance, human services, procurement, legal practice, transportation, design, and more. Spring 2026 Workshop Series Subscribe to InnovateUS updates or visit innovate-us.org for the full schedule Below is a high-level snapshot of the series launching this semester, with more detail in our full course catalog and registration links forthcoming. Most Requested: Leadership Skills Begins Jan 26 | runs Jan–Jun Some of our most celebrated instructors return with sessions on organizational transformation, policy analysis, crisis leadership, partnership strategies, and change management. Amplify: Mastering Public Communication in the AI Age Co-hosted with Northeastern University's Burnes Center for Social Change Begins Jan 12, 2026 | Runs Jan–Mar Public leaders learn to communicate clearly, credibly, and inclusively in a fast-changing information environment. This season focuses on trustworthy messaging, data storytelling, and responsible use of AI for public communication. The Prompting Lab: Real Prompts, Real Challenges, All Platforms Co-hosted with Davyd Smith, Office of Information Technology, State of Colorado; Jorge Valens, Miami-Dade County IT; and Harrison McRae, Office of Administration, State of Pennsylvania. Begins January 16, 2026 | Runs Jan–June, every Friday at 2 PM ET A weekly, hands-on practice lab where public professionals tackle real AI tasks using GPT, Claude, Copilot, Gemini, and more. You can bring your workflows, experiment with peers, and learn what works. Prediction, Automation & Decision-Making with AI: Risks and Opportunities Co-hosted with Princeton Center for Information Technology Policy. Begins Jan 21 | Runs Jan - February A practical guide to what AI can and cannot do in government. Participants learn how predictive tools actually work, why "prediction isn't intelligence," how to evaluate vendor claims, and how global regulations are evolving. AI for Public Legal Professionals Begins February 9, 2026 | Runs February - April How attorneys general's offices, public defenders, and government legal teams can use AI responsibly, while meeting ethical obligations and preparing for new standards. Opening Data for AI Innovation Begins February 2026 How to build AI-ready public data: interoperable, accessible, responsibly governed. Includes case studies from DC, Indiana, and federal open-data leaders. AI and Public Transportation: Smarter, Safer, More Efficient Mobility Begins March 2026 Exploring how transit agencies use AI to support safety, operations, planning, and rider experience, always with human judgment at the center. AI and Human Services: Innovating to Serve People Better Co-hosted with the Center for Civic Futures Begins March 2026 A deeply human-centered series on applying AI in eligibility, case management, service design, language access, and community engagement—co-hosted with the Center for Civic Futures. Public AI – Buying & Building for Civic Use Begins March 2026 A foundational series on the emerging movement for "public AI": open, interoperable, accountable systems built as public infrastructure. Covers procurement strategies, governance, vendor lock-in, international models, and the public option for AI. Human-Centered Design Begins March 2026 How to redesign services around people's real needs, including where AI can help reduce friction, not increase it. Data Analysis & Visualization for Public Professionals (AI-Assisted) Begins March 2026 How to use AI tools to clean, analyze, and visualize public-sector data—especially for evidence-based decision-making. AI for Smarter Procurement Co-hosted with Partners for Public Good Begins April 2026 How AI can support clearer RFPs, better bid evaluation, contract monitoring, and more transparent procurement. AI for Literacy Achievement Begins April 2026 Returns with a new series focused on how policy, governance, and system-level decisions shape the responsible use of AI to improve educational outcomes at scale. The Elephants in the AI Room: Bias, Displacement, Sustainability Begins May 2026 A series dedicated to the tough questions: bias mitigation, workforce impacts, and the environmental footprint of AI. AI and Energy Begins June 2026 Understanding the environmental footprint of AI, its sustainability implications, and what public policy needs to keep pace. Using AI for Digital Accessibility Begins June 2026 Practical tools and techniques for evaluating and improving accessibility in public digital services. Join Us This Spring The Spring 2026 season reflects what public servants told us they need most: clarity, practical skills, and a space to ask hard questions without hype. Whether you're evaluating AI tools, redesigning services, communicating with the public, or leading organizational change, there's a workshop designed for your work. Registration opens in early January. Subscribe to InnovateUS updates or visit innovate-us.org for the full schedule.
